title: A motion test must assert the running animation's timing, read after the transition is finished
rule: When a Playwright test proves a duration or curve of a view transition or CSS animation, read the running animations (`document.getAnimations()` filtered on the pseudo-element or element, `getComputedTiming().duration`), not the token (`getPropertyValue('--fm-motion-*')`): the token keeps its value when the rule that applies it is deleted. Fill the probe in `transition.ready.then(...)` and read it only after a wait that comes later (the transition's class or attribute being removed on `finished`), never right after a state change made in the update callback. Check that the mutation 'delete the timing rule' fails the test.
rationale: E47.2 (#483): the 200 ms theme crossfade test read `--fm-motion-move` (always 200ms) and passed with the timing rule removed; the first fix then read the record before `ready` could have filled it, a flake on the slow macOS runner.
